We need propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <=9999 (we don't have price data, assume buyable). Need to construct route JSON.

Target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide linking to an aniline (anilide). So we can think disconnection: break sulfonamide S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. Also break amide bond to give acid and aniline. Also break C=C double bond maybe via Heck? Simpler: retrosynthesis: target from sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline bearing the rest? Actually sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O)Ar2. So we can get sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) reacting with aniline (Ar-NH-). So step1: sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the rest of molecule after N attached). The rest is an aniline attached to phenyl with trans-α,β-unsaturated amide linking to another aniline? Wait structure: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to tolyl via N? Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So central N is attached to tolyl (para methyl phenyl) and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl which has the unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we have two aniline nitrogens: one attached to sulfonyl (sulfonamide) and one at the amide terminus (anilide). So disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: use p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline) + aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl where Ar is phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide). So step1: sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) + p-toluidine -> target.

2) For Ar-SO2Cl precursor: could be made from corresponding phenyl sulfonic acid or from chlorosulfonation of phenyl? But we can also consider making the unsaturated amide part first: start from aniline (c3ccccc3N) and cinnamic acid derivative? The unsaturated amide: /C=C/C(=O)N- attached to phenyl (Ar). So we can form amide via coupling of aniline (c3ccccc3N) with trans-cinnamic acid (C=CC(=O)O) attached to phenyl? Actually the amide is attached to phenyl via the carbonyl carbon: phenyl-CO-NH-aniline? Wait SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. The carbonyl attached to N of aniline, and the carbonyl carbon attached to the C=C chain which is attached to phenyl (c2ccc...). So we have phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline. So we can make that via amide coupling of aniline with trans-cinnamic acid (phenyl-CH=CH-COOH). So step2: trans-cinnamic acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> unsaturated amide (phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline). That's commercially available? trans-cinnamic acid is buyable. Aniline is buyable.

Then step3: sulfonyl chloride formation: need phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (the product) to be sulfonylated? Actually we need to attach sulfonyl group to that phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). So we need to convert that phenyl to sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) then react with p-toluidine. But sulfonyl chloride is derived from sulfonation of the phenyl (maybe via chlorosulfonic acid). However we can consider using commercially available aryl sulfonyl chloride that already has the unsaturated amide attached? Might not be available. Alternative route: first form sulfonamide then amide? Could reverse order: first sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) + p-toluidine gives sulfonamide attached to phenyl. Then later amide formation on that phenyl? But the amide is on the same phenyl (the sulfonyl phenyl). So after sulfonamide formation, we have phenyl-SO2-NH-p-tolyl. The phenyl also needs to have the unsaturated amide substituent at para position? Actually the sulfonyl phenyl is substituted at para with the unsaturated amide chain. So we need to have that substituent before sulfonylation. So we need a phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide (para) and then sulfonyl chloride at that phenyl? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl via S=O2Cl attached to the phenyl (Ar-SO2Cl). The sulfonyl phenyl is the one bearing the unsaturated amide at para? In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl (c2ccc...). The phenyl has the unsaturated amide substituent at para relative to the sulfonyl? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl via S, and the phenyl has the unsaturated amide substituent at para (maybe). So we need a phenyl with that substituent, then convert to sulfonyl chloride (by chlorosulfonation at the position where sulfonyl attaches (the position currently attached to S). That is a sulfonyl chloride attached directly to phenyl (Ar-SO2Cl). So we need phenyl with para unsaturated amide, then chlorosulfonate to get sulfonyl chloride, then react with p-toluidine.

Thus route:

Step A (final): p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) -> target sulfonamide.

Step B: Prepare aryl sulfonyl chloride from aryl (Ar-H) bearing para unsaturated amide substituent via chlorosulfonation (ClSO2Cl reagent). But we can consider using commercially available aryl sulfonyl chloride with that substituent? Likely not. So we need to generate it. However we can treat as a reaction step: chlorosulfonation of aryl (Ar-H) to give Ar-SO2Cl. So we need aryl precursor: phenyl with para unsaturated amide (Ar-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline). That's the same as product of step2.

Thus step2: Synthesize that aryl unsaturated amide (Ar-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline) via amide coupling of trans-cinnamic acid (or its derivative) with aniline. The phenyl is the same phenyl (c2ccc...). So we need trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) and aniline (commercial). Reaction: amidation (e.g., using coupling reagents). So step2 yields the aryl unsaturated amide.

Step3: Chlorosulfonation of that aryl unsaturated amide to give aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline-SO2Cl). Then step1 (final) sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine.

Thus total steps: 3 steps (amide formation, chlorosulfonation, sulfonamide formation). Leaves: trans-cinnamic acid, aniline, p-toluidine (or p-toluidine is Cc1ccc(N)cc1). All are buyable (we checked). Also need chlorosulfonic acid (ClSO3H) maybe not needed as leaf? It's reagent, not leaf. Leaves are only starting materials (commercial chemicals). So we have three leaves: trans-cinnamic acid (C=CC(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1), aniline (Nc1ccccc1), p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1). All buyable.

Now need to construct JSON route.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We need to find appropriate templates via search. Let's search for amide formation (functional_groups_formed: amide).
